name: Transformations
blurb: Decompose the modification request into verb-shaped transformations over discovered targets — confirmed by the user bottom-up, tier by tier.
directive: **Transformations** — decompose the modification request into TRANSFORMATIONS (the modification counterpart to features): each is a verb + target + delta + invariants + blast radius. Verbs (fixed taxonomy): rename | extract | split | merge | move | replace | upgrade | restyle | remove | optimize | harden — each has a known recipe + verification pattern. prompt:
Decompose the modification request into TRANSFORMATIONS — the modification counterpart to
features. Creation decomposes into features; modification decomposes into transformations, and
each one is small enough to execute, verify, and confirm on its own.

THE UNIT — every transformation carries:
  • verb — from the fixed taxonomy: rename | extract | split | merge | move | replace | upgrade |
    restyle | remove | optimize | harden. The verb is what makes the chunk easy: each has a known
    recipe + verification pattern.
  • target — the identified piece of the EXISTING system. Targets are DISCOVERED: scan the linked
    repos and name the real files/components you found (target.description + target.files). Never
    invent a target.
  • delta — the from-state → to-state.
  • invariants — what must NOT change (the modification twin of acceptance criteria). "existing
    tests pass" is the floor; add the stated invariants a reviewer can check.
  • owns — the blast radius (owned globs). Transformations collide on files more than features do,
    so sequencing waves matter more than parallelism.
  • tier — the composition tier for the BOTTOM-UP confirm queue: 0 = the most basic primitives,
    then composites, then layouts/pages. The user confirms tier by tier, so nothing is built on
    unreviewed foundations.
  • dependsOn — sequencing waves (foundation before fan-out): a row lists the ids it builds on.
  • provenance (optional) — the recipe that generated it ("migrate-to-kit" |
    "extract-and-abstract") + the evidence found while scanning; kitContribution marks a gap-fill
    that belongs to the kit; spec is the KitNode render spec the pane previews LIVE — REQUIRED on
    every gap-fill row (kitContribution: true), optional elsewhere (see AUTHORING THE PREVIEW SPEC).

RECORD the list with `bsc plan transformation add` (JSON on stdin — one object or an array). A
WORKED EXAMPLE with the exact shape — two rows: a migrate-to-kit replace (its optional `spec` is
omitted here; add one when the kit target has a specimen to preview) and an extract:

echo '[
  {
    "id": "replace-bespoke-buttons",
    "verb": "replace",
    "title": "Replace the bespoke dashboard buttons with the kit Button",
    "target": {
      "description": "the 14 hand-rolled button components found across the dashboard screens",
      "files": ["src/components/SaveButton.tsx", "src/components/DangerButton.tsx"]
    },
    "delta": "each bespoke button renders through the kit Button with the matching variant; the bespoke files are deleted",
    "invariants": ["existing tests pass", "every click handler keeps its current behavior", "keyboard focus order is unchanged"],
    "owns": ["src/components/*Button*.tsx"],
    "tier": 0,
    "provenance": { "recipe": "migrate-to-kit", "evidence": ["src/components/SaveButton.tsx (12 usages)", "src/components/DangerButton.tsx (3 usages)"] },
    "kitContribution": false
  },
  {
    "id": "extract-form-field",
    "verb": "extract",
    "title": "Extract the duplicated form-field scaffold into one shared FormField",
    "target": {
      "description": "the label + error + input scaffold duplicated across the 6 form screens"
    },
    "delta": "one shared FormField component; the 6 form screens render through it and the copies are deleted",
    "invariants": ["existing tests pass", "validation messages render identically on every form"],
    "owns": ["src/shared/FormField.tsx", "src/screens/forms/"],
    "dependsOn": ["replace-bespoke-buttons"],
    "tier": 1,
    "provenance": { "recipe": "extract-and-abstract", "evidence": ["src/screens/forms/Login.tsx", "src/screens/forms/Signup.tsx"] }
  }
]' | bsc plan transformation add

The write is VALIDATED at set-time (#2395): a known verb, a discovered target.description, a
non-empty delta, non-empty invariants + owns, an integer tier >= 0, and — on a gap-fill row
(kitContribution: true) — a spec object; a malformed row is rejected with a field-level error and
the whole batch is refused (the stored list is untouched).
Iterate with `bsc plan transformation list` / `get <id>` / `update <id>` (JSON on stdin).

RECIPES — the composite transforms that GENERATE the list (a generated row records its recipe
in provenance.recipe). When the modification request matches one, run its playbook. The playbooks
below expand the canonical `@data/transformations/taxonomy.json` recipes[].steps — the two stay in
lockstep (drift-tested).

MIGRATE-TO-KIT — migrate a linked frontend onto the component kit (the flagship):
  1. Enumerate the kit FIRST — every component, its whenUse/whenNot guidance, and its variants:
       bsc ui kit list        # the kits: { id, name, stack }
       bsc ui list --full     # every component IN FULL: variants, props, whenUse, whenNot
       bsc ui get <id>        # one component verbatim
       bsc ui shapes          # the data-shape vocabulary -> each shape's ideal components
     (`bsc component ...` is the same surface, a deprecated alias — use `bsc ui`.)
  2. Scan the linked frontend for its components and their usage sites (Glob/Grep over the repo)
     and COUNT the usages per component — the counts are the evidence.
  3. Bucket EVERY finding: direct-mappable (a kit component covers it as-is) ·
     mappable-with-adaptation (covered with a variant/prop delta) · no-equivalent (nothing in the
     kit covers it).
  4. No-equivalent CLUSTERS — >=2 similar bespoke implementations, or pages needing a missing
     Layout template — become GAP-FILL rows: kitContribution: true, verb "extract", the tier of
     the thing being BUILT, evidence = the bespoke instances with their usage counts. (A one-off
     with no cluster is a plain migration judgment call, not a kit gap.)
  5. Migration rows list their gap-fill builds in dependsOn — the gap-fill lands first.
  6. Assign tiers per the taxonomy: 0 primitives · 1 composites · 2 layouts · 3 pages.
  7. Write the WHOLE list in ONE `bsc plan transformation add` batch.

A gap-fill row and its dependent migration row, concretely (the same add-batch shape):

echo '[
  {
    "id": "gap-fill-datagrid",
    "verb": "extract",
    "title": "Gap-fill: build the missing DataGrid kit component",
    "target": {
      "description": "a no-equivalent cluster: 3 similar bespoke sortable tables with no kit counterpart",
      "files": ["src/reports/ReportTable.tsx", "src/admin/UserTable.tsx", "src/billing/InvoiceTable.tsx"]
    },
    "delta": "no kit table exists; a DataGrid kit component (sortable columns + row selection) generalizes all 3 bespoke tables",
    "invariants": ["existing tests pass", "the new component validates against the kit contract (bsc ui validate)"],
    "owns": ["src/shared/ui/data/DataGrid.tsx"],
    "tier": 1,
    "provenance": { "recipe": "migrate-to-kit", "evidence": ["src/reports/ReportTable.tsx (9 usages)", "src/admin/UserTable.tsx (5 usages)", "src/billing/InvoiceTable.tsx (2 usages)"] },
    "kitContribution": true,
    "spec": {
      "kind": "card",
      "tone": "var(--accent)",
      "header": { "kind": "header", "title": "DataGrid", "hint": "sortable + selectable" },
      "children": [
        { "kind": "row", "label": "Columns", "children": [
          { "kind": "tag", "label": "Name", "tone": "accent" },
          { "kind": "tag", "label": "Status", "tone": "accent" },
          { "kind": "tag", "label": "Amount", "tone": "accent" }
        ] },
        { "kind": "row", "label": "Select all", "children": [{ "kind": "toggle", "bind": "selectAll" }] },
        { "kind": "text", "text": "3 rows selected", "tone": "muted" },
        { "kind": "field", "control": "text", "label": "Filter rows", "bind": "filter", "placeholder": "Search rows" },
        { "kind": "button", "variant": "primary", "label": "Export", "action": "export" }
      ]
    }
  },
  {
    "id": "migrate-tables-to-datagrid",
    "verb": "replace",
    "title": "Migrate the 3 bespoke tables onto DataGrid",
    "target": {
      "description": "the 3 bespoke sortable tables the gap-fill generalizes",
      "files": ["src/reports/ReportTable.tsx", "src/admin/UserTable.tsx", "src/billing/InvoiceTable.tsx"]
    },
    "delta": "each bespoke table renders through the kit DataGrid and its bespoke implementation is deleted",
    "invariants": ["existing tests pass", "sort order and row selection behave identically on every table"],
    "owns": ["src/reports/ReportTable.tsx", "src/admin/UserTable.tsx", "src/billing/InvoiceTable.tsx"],
    "dependsOn": ["gap-fill-datagrid"],
    "tier": 1,
    "provenance": { "recipe": "migrate-to-kit", "evidence": ["src/reports/ReportTable.tsx (9 usages)", "src/admin/UserTable.tsx (5 usages)", "src/billing/InvoiceTable.tsx (2 usages)"] },
    "kitContribution": false
  }
]' | bsc plan transformation add

EXTRACT-AND-ABSTRACT — N similar implementations become one shared abstraction (the codified
refactor workflow):
  1. Find the N similar bespoke implementations (Glob/Grep; record each with its usage count —
     that is the evidence).
  2. Record ONE extract row for the shared abstraction — the FOUNDATION, at the lower tier.
  3. Record N replace rows, one per original, each listing the extract row in dependsOn.
  4. Fold delete-the-original into each replace row's delta — no separate remove rows.
  5. Sequence foundation-first waves: the extract lands, then the replaces fan out in parallel.

AUTHORING THE PREVIEW SPEC — the pane renders each row's `spec` LIVE (through the kit's specimen
renderer), so the spec is HOW the user sees a component before deciding on it. A `spec` is a KitNode
tree of the 8 kinds (card / header / field / button / row / toggle / tag / text) — the same contract
`bsc ui validate` enforces; author it, pipe it through `bsc ui validate`, and fix any error before
adding the row. Study the shape of the DataGrid card example above (a `card` with a `header` and
representative `children`) and compose the sketch from those existing kinds — it is a PROPOSAL
sketch of the component, not its final code.
  • REQUIRED on every gap-fill row (kitContribution: true): the user is deciding whether to build a
    NEW component, so they must SEE a representative sketch of it. A gap-fill row without a `spec`
    is rejected at set-time (#2395).
  • ENCOURAGED on a direct/adaptation migration row when the kit target has a natural node form (a
    Button, a field, a small card) — render the target so the user sees what the bespoke code
    becomes.
  • The preview is READ-ONLY in the pane (no bindings fire — the planner owns edits, #2382); keep
    the spec small and representative, a handful of nodes that convey the component at a glance.

HARD RULES:
  • Targets are discovered by scanning, never invented — every target names something the scan
    actually found.
  • Order bottom-up: tier 0 primitives first, composites next, pages last; sequence file
    collisions with dependsOn (foundation before fan-out).
  • The USER confirms each item in the pane, one at a time, bottom-up — NEVER run
    `bsc plan transformation confirm` yourself, and never treat an item as approved until the
    user has confirmed it.
  • When the user describes a change conversationally, UPDATE the row
    (`bsc plan transformation update <id>`) — the item re-presents in the queue for a fresh
    confirm.

Then write the prose summary to transformations.md via the section-file flow like the other
stages — the discovered targets, the tier ordering, and the wave sequencing.

Gate: every transformation confirmed, bottom-up; the user confirms the stage.

substeps.label: Discover the targets
substeps.gate: every target names real, scanned files — nothing invented
substeps.prompt:
Scan the linked repos and DISCOVER the targets the modification request touches — the real
files and components, never invented ones. For each candidate record what it is
(target.description), where it lives (target.files), and the evidence you found (usage counts,
duplicated implementations, bespoke variants). This scan is what makes every downstream row
honest: a transformation over an invented target is unexecutable.
When the request is a MIGRATE-TO-KIT, enumerate the kit FIRST (`bsc ui kit list` ·
`bsc ui list --full` — whenUse/whenNot + variants · `bsc ui shapes`) so every finding
is bucketed against the real kit: direct-mappable / mappable-with-adaptation /
no-equivalent.

substeps.label: Decompose into transformations
substeps.gate: the list is recorded via `bsc plan transformation add` (verb + target + delta + invariants + owns + tier, validated)
substeps.prompt:
Decompose the request into one row per transformation: a verb from the taxonomy (rename |
extract | split | merge | move | replace | upgrade | restyle | remove | optimize | harden), the
discovered target, the delta (from-state → to-state), the invariants (what must NOT change —
existing tests pass is the floor), the owns globs (the blast radius), and the composition tier
(0 = primitives … N = pages). Sequence file collisions with dependsOn — foundation before
fan-out. Record the rows with `bsc plan transformation add` (the stage prompt carries the full
worked example); the write validates at set-time (#2395) with field-level errors.
When a recipe generated the rows (migrate-to-kit / extract-and-abstract), record it
in provenance.recipe; no-equivalent CLUSTERS become kitContribution gap-fill rows built
FIRST, with each dependent migration sequenced on its gap-fill via dependsOn (the stage
prompt carries the recipe playbooks and a concrete gap-fill example).

substeps.label: The bottom-up confirm queue
substeps.gate: every transformation confirmed by the user, bottom-up
substeps.prompt:
The user now confirms the queue in the pane, bottom-up — tier 0 primitives first, composites
next, pages last. YOU never confirm: an item is pending or confirmed, nothing else, and only the
user flips it. When the user describes a change conversationally, update that row
(`bsc plan transformation update <id>`) — it re-presents in the queue for a fresh confirm. The
stage gate passes when every item is confirmed.
